notes:
Summary: QuarrySearch builds an enterprise-grade legal/compliance search product used by regulatory teams. Primary pain: scaling semantic search + reranking on large corpora (contracts, policies). Currently prototyping hybrid BM25 + embeddings flow. Key asked for Redwood: vector DB connectors w/ efficient bulk ingest, incremental upserts, and a reranker hook to avoid unnecessary token spend.

What they told AE (Maya) on 10/18 call: "We need sub-200ms median query latency for top-5 results across 10M+ indexed docs and predictable cost per query. If reranking doubles token usage we need a fallback cheap rerank (lightweight cross-encoder) or candidate pruning."

Technical requirements (quoted/notes):
- Index scale: aiming for 10M-50M small-doc chunks (1-3 paragraphs) -> ~2-8B vectors.
- Query SLA: median latency 50-200ms for vector lookup + rerank stage target < 350ms end-to-end for interactive UI.
- Cost sensitivity: want cost per query predictable; willing to trade higher vector index memory for lower LM token cost via smaller reranker model.
- Connector wishlist: bulk ingest with resume, per-doc metadata mapping, hybrid search API (BM25 + vector), support for HNSW configs + shard control, namespace/collection isolation per-customer, incremental upserts with tombstone support, and low-latency streaming upsert for near-real-time ingestion.
- DB options under evaluation: Pinecone (managed), Weaviate (open, rich metadata), pgvector (SQL integration with existing infra), Elastic Vector plugin (consolidation with existing ES clusters). They asked specifically for recommended default connector settings per DB (batch size, vector dims handling, quantization settings).
- Security/compliance: traffic must traverse VPC peering; embedding keys stored in KMS; audit logs for every upsert and query; retention controls to expire vectors after legal hold removal.

POC scope discussed:
- Phase 1: Bulk ingest 10M doc chunks (drive sample + S3), validate namespace isolation. Friday test window agreed.
- Phase 2: End-to-end query profiling: measure cosine/L2 lookup latencies, candidate set sizes (k=100), then run reranker (small cross-encoder) to evaluate token cost tradeoffs.
- Phase 3: Tune batching and caching (prefix caching + query-level LRU) to hit cost/latency target.

Stakeholders: CTO - Arjun Patel (final signoff), Head of Search - Fiona Blake (technical lead for POC), Data Eng - Thomas Ng (ingest pipelines), Legal/Compliance - Rebecca Meyer (data residency + retention).

- 2024-10-08: Intro call (AE Maya) - basic needs, demo requested.
- 2024-10-12: Demo w/ SE Diego (showed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs).
- 2024-10-18: Deep technical call (fireflies id above) on ingestion scale and reranking economics.

Quotes / call snippets: "If we can't guarantee cost per query within a factor of 2, procurement will push back." — Fiona B.

Also prepare a flow diagram for fallback routing: primary vector search -> small reranker -> full LLM fallback only if confidence low.
